meta.subject: math
meta.description: Algebra facts: equations, slope, quadratic formula, factoring, exponents, functions, inequalities, systems, radicals, polynomials

facts.statement: An equation is a mathematical statement that two expressions are equal, using the = sign
To solve an equation, isolate the variable by performing the same operation on both sides
A linear equation in one variable has the form ax + b = c, where a, b, and c are constants and x is the variable
The solution to an equation is the value of the variable that makes the equation true
Inverse operations undo each other: addition undoes subtraction, multiplication undoes division
When solving, whatever you do to one side of the equation you must do to the other side to keep it balanced
A coefficient is the number multiplied by a variable: in 5x, the coefficient is 5
A constant term has no variable: in 3x + 7, the constant is 7
Like terms have the same variable raised to the same power: 3x and 5x are like terms; 3x and 3x^2 are not
To solve 2x + 5 = 13: subtract 5 from both sides (2x = 8), then divide both sides by 2 (x = 4)
An equation with no solution is called a contradiction: 2x + 3 = 2x + 7 has no solution
An identity is true for all values of the variable: 2(x+3) = 2x+6 is always true

common_errors.wrong: you can add to one side without adding to the other
common_errors.correct: Both sides must remain equal. Any operation must be performed on both sides.

common_errors.wrong: 5x means 5 + x
common_errors.correct: 5x means 5 multiplied by x, not 5 plus x. In algebra, a number next to a variable indicates multiplication.
When combining like terms, add the coefficients: 3x + 5x = 8x, not 8x^2.

common_errors.wrong: to solve 2x = 10, subtract 2 from both sides
common_errors.correct: Since x is multiplied by 2, use the inverse: divide both sides by 2 to get x = 5.

facts.statement: An inequality uses <, >, <=, or >= to compare expressions: x > 5 means x is greater than 5
When multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number, the inequality sign must be reversed
The solution to an inequality is a range of values, not a single value: x > 3 includes 4, 5, 3.5, 100, etc.
On a number line, an open circle means the endpoint is NOT included (< or >); a closed circle means it IS included (<= or >=)
A compound inequality uses AND or OR: 2 < x < 5 means x is between 2 and 5
Absolute value inequality |x| < a means -a < x < a; |x| > a means x < -a or x > a
Interval notation: (2, 5) means 2 < x < 5; [2, 5] means 2 <= x <= 5

common_errors.wrong: when you multiply an inequality by a negative, the sign stays the same
common_errors.correct: You MUST flip the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative: -2x > 6 becomes x < -3.

common_errors.wrong: |x| < -3 has solutions
common_errors.correct: Absolute value is always non-negative, so |x| < -3 has no solution. No number's absolute value is negative.

common_errors.wrong: x > 3 AND x < 1 includes many numbers
common_errors.correct: There is no number that is both greater than 3 AND less than 1. This compound inequality has no solution.

facts.statement: Slope-intercept form is y = mx + b, where m is the slope and b is the y-intercept
Slope measures the steepness of a line, calculated as rise over run: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
A positive slope means the line goes up from left to right; a negative slope means it goes down
A slope of zero means a horizontal line; an undefined slope means a vertical line
The y-intercept is the point where the line crosses the y-axis, occurring when x = 0
Parallel lines have the same slope but different y-intercepts
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other: m1 x m2 = -1
Point-slope form is y - y1 = m(x - x1), useful when you know a point and the slope
Standard form of a linear equation is Ax + By = C, where A, B, and C are integers
The x-intercept is the point where the line crosses the x-axis, occurring when y = 0
The slope between (1, 2) and (4, 8) is (8-2)/(4-1) = 6/3 = 2
A line with equation y = 3 is horizontal with slope 0; a line with equation x = 3 is vertical with undefined slope

common_errors.wrong: slope is run over rise
common_errors.correct: Slope is rise over run: vertical change divided by horizontal change (y2-y1)/(x2-x1).

common_errors.wrong: a vertical line has a slope of zero
common_errors.correct: A vertical line has an undefined slope. A horizontal line has a slope of zero.

common_errors.wrong: parallel lines have different slopes
common_errors.correct: Parallel lines have the same slope. If they had different slopes, they would eventually intersect.

common_errors.wrong: perpendicular lines have opposite slopes
common_errors.correct: Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals: if one has slope 2, the other has slope -1/2.

common_errors.wrong: the y-intercept is always positive
common_errors.correct: The y-intercept can be positive, negative, or zero. It is simply where the line crosses the y-axis.

facts.statement: A system of linear equations is two or more equations with the same variables
The solution of a system is the point (x, y) that satisfies all equations simultaneously
Substitution method: solve one equation for a variable, then substitute into the other equation
Elimination method: add or subtract equations to eliminate one variable
Graphically, the solution of a system is where the lines intersect
A consistent system has at least one solution; an inconsistent system (parallel lines) has no solution
A dependent system has infinitely many solutions (the equations describe the same line)
Two lines with different slopes always intersect at exactly one point

common_errors.wrong: every system of two equations has exactly one solution
common_errors.correct: A system can have one solution (intersecting lines), no solution (parallel lines), or infinitely many (same line).

common_errors.wrong: you only need to solve for one variable in a system
common_errors.correct: You must find values for ALL variables. The solution is an ordered pair (x, y).

common_errors.wrong: parallel lines eventually meet
common_errors.correct: Parallel lines have the same slope and never intersect. The system has no solution.

facts.statement: A quadratic equation has the standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0, where a is not 0
The quadratic formula is x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / (2a)
The discriminant b^2 - 4ac determines the number of real solutions: positive = 2, zero = 1, negative = 0 real solutions
The graph of a quadratic equation is a parabola that opens upward if a > 0 and downward if a < 0
The vertex of a parabola y = ax^2 + bx + c is at x = -b/(2a)
The roots (or zeros) of a quadratic are the x-values where the parabola crosses the x-axis
Vertex form of a quadratic is y = a(x - h)^2 + k, where (h, k) is the vertex
The axis of symmetry of a parabola is the vertical line x = -b/(2a), passing through the vertex
Completing the square: x^2 + 6x + ? = (x+3)^2, so add 9. The number to add is (b/2)^2
Zero Product Property: if ab = 0, then a = 0 or b = 0. Used to solve factored quadratics

common_errors.wrong: every quadratic equation has two real solutions
common_errors.correct: A quadratic can have 0, 1, or 2 real solutions depending on the discriminant.

common_errors.wrong: the vertex is always at x = 0
common_errors.correct: The vertex is at x = -b/(2a). It is at x=0 only when b=0.

common_errors.wrong: a parabola always opens upward
common_errors.correct: If the coefficient a is negative, the parabola opens downward.

common_errors.wrong: completing the square means dividing the equation by 2
common_errors.correct: Completing the square means adding (b/2)^2 to create a perfect square trinomial.

common_errors.wrong: if x^2 = 9, then x = 3
common_errors.correct: If x^2 = 9, then x = 3 or x = -3. Square roots produce both positive and negative solutions.

facts.statement: An exponent tells how many times to multiply a base by itself: 2^3 = 2 x 2 x 2 = 8
Any nonzero number raised to the power of 0 equals 1: a^0 = 1
Product rule: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n) -- when multiplying same bases, add exponents
Quotient rule: a^m / a^n = a^(m-n) -- when dividing same bases, subtract exponents
Power rule: (a^m)^n = a^(m*n) -- when raising a power to a power, multiply exponents
A negative exponent means the reciprocal: a^(-n) = 1/(a^n)
Scientific notation writes numbers as a x 10^n where 1 <= a < 10: 3,200 = 3.2 x 10^3
A fractional exponent means a root: a^(1/2) = sqrt(a), a^(1/3) = cube root of a
Power of a product: (ab)^n = a^n x b^n
Power of a quotient: (a/b)^n = a^n / b^n
The square root of a product: sqrt(ab) = sqrt(a) x sqrt(b)
Exponential growth: y = a(1+r)^t, where r is the growth rate and t is time
Exponential decay: y = a(1-r)^t, where r is the decay rate and t is time

common_errors.wrong: 2^3 means 2 x 3 = 6
common_errors.correct: 2^3 means 2 multiplied by itself 3 times: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.
0^0 is commonly defined as 1 in most mathematical contexts, though it is technically indeterminate.

common_errors.wrong: when multiplying exponents with the same base, multiply the exponents
common_errors.correct: When multiplying same bases, ADD the exponents: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n). You multiply exponents when raising a power to a power.

common_errors.wrong: a negative exponent makes the number negative
common_errors.correct: A negative exponent means the reciprocal: 2^(-3) = 1/8, not -8.

common_errors.wrong: sqrt(a + b) = sqrt(a) + sqrt(b)
common_errors.correct: Square roots do NOT distribute over addition. sqrt(9+16) = sqrt(25) = 5, but sqrt(9)+sqrt(16) = 3+4 = 7.

facts.statement: Factoring is the process of breaking an expression into a product of simpler expressions
To factor out the GCF, find the largest factor common to all terms and divide each term by it
The difference of squares pattern: a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)
FOIL (First, Outer, Inner, Last) is a method for multiplying two binomials: (a+b)(c+d) = ac + ad + bc + bd
A perfect square trinomial: a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = (a + b)^2
To factor x^2 + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b
Sum of cubes: a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)
Difference of cubes: a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)
Factoring by grouping: group terms in pairs, factor out common factors from each pair, then factor the common binomial
A polynomial is fully factored when no factor can be factored further over the integers

common_errors.wrong: a^2 + b^2 can be factored as (a+b)(a+b)
common_errors.correct: The SUM of two squares a^2 + b^2 cannot be factored over the real numbers. Only the DIFFERENCE of squares factors: a^2 - b^2 = (a+b)(a-b).
(a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2. The middle term 2ab must not be forgotten.
Find two numbers that multiply to 6 AND add to 5: 2 and 3. So x^2 + 5x + 6 = (x+2)(x+3).
(a-b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2, not a^2 - b^2. The difference of squares a^2 - b^2 = (a+b)(a-b).

facts.statement: A function assigns exactly one output to each input: f(x) = 2x + 3 means for input x, output is 2x + 3
The domain is the set of all possible input values (x-values); the range is the set of all possible output values (y-values)
The vertical line test: if any vertical line crosses a graph more than once, it is NOT a function
f(3) means 'evaluate the function at x = 3' by substituting 3 for x
A linear function has the form f(x) = mx + b and its graph is a straight line
Composition of functions: (f o g)(x) = f(g(x)) means apply g first, then apply f to the result
An inverse function f^(-1) undoes f: if f(2) = 5, then f^(-1)(5) = 2
A function is one-to-one if each output comes from exactly one input (passes the horizontal line test)
Common function types: linear, quadratic, absolute value, exponential, logarithmic, polynomial
The graph of f(x) + k shifts the graph up k units; f(x) - k shifts it down k units

common_errors.wrong: f(x) means f times x
common_errors.correct: f(x) is function notation meaning 'the output of function f when the input is x.' It is NOT multiplication.

common_errors.wrong: a circle is a function
common_errors.correct: A circle fails the vertical line test: for most x-values, there are two y-values. It is NOT a function.

common_errors.wrong: every function has an inverse function
common_errors.correct: Only one-to-one functions (passing the horizontal line test) have inverse functions.

common_errors.wrong: f(a+b) = f(a) + f(b) for any function
common_errors.correct: This is only true for linear functions of the form f(x) = kx. In general, f(a+b) does not equal f(a)+f(b).

facts.statement: A polynomial is a sum of terms where each term has a variable raised to a non-negative integer power
The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable: 3x^4 + 2x^2 - 1 has degree 4
Monomial = 1 term, binomial = 2 terms, trinomial = 3 terms
The leading coefficient is the coefficient of the highest-degree term
A polynomial of degree n has at most n real roots (zeros)
The Remainder Theorem: when polynomial p(x) is divided by (x-a), the remainder is p(a)
The Factor Theorem: (x-a) is a factor of p(x) if and only if p(a) = 0
End behavior: odd-degree polynomials go in opposite directions at each end; even-degree go in the same direction

common_errors.wrong: the degree of 5x^2 + 3x^3 is 2 because that term comes first
common_errors.correct: The degree is determined by the highest power, not the order written. Degree is 3 from the 3x^3 term.

common_errors.wrong: a polynomial of degree 3 always has 3 real roots
common_errors.correct: A degree-3 polynomial has AT MOST 3 real roots. It always has at least 1 real root, but the others may be complex.

common_errors.wrong: you can have a variable in the denominator in a polynomial
common_errors.correct: Polynomials only have non-negative integer exponents. 3/x = 3x^(-1) is NOT a polynomial term.
